misconception.text: The energy levels of an atom are spread evenly.

correction.text: They are not. The levels get closer together as the energy rises, and the ground state is separated by a large gap.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The energy of a photon depends on how bright the light is.

correction.text: It depends on the frequency. The brightness tells you how many photons there are.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: String theory is a confirmed theory of everything.

correction.text: It is a promising idea that is still being tested, and it is not part of the standard model.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: Dark matter has been seen directly.

correction.text: It has not. Its presence is inferred from the rotation of galaxies and from the lensing of light, not from a direct detection.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: A tracer is used to see the shape of an organ.

correction.text: It shows how the organ works, by following where the tracer goes in the body.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The dose from a tracer is the same however the tracer is given.

correction.text: It depends on the activity, the half life, and how long it stays in the body.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The standard model explains every particle there is.

correction.text: It explains the particles we have found so far. Gravity is not in it, and the matter and antimatter imbalance is not explained either.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: Particles and antiparticles are the same thing with the opposite charge.

correction.text: They have the same mass and opposite charge, and when they meet they annihilate into photons.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: An electron is a small ball that orbits the nucleus.

correction.text: It has no orbit. It occupies a quantum state, and the orbit picture is only a picture.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: A photon is a particle and never behaves as a wave.

correction.text: It behaves as a particle when it is absorbed or emitted, and as a wave when it passes through a double slit.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The half life of a radioactive sample is a fixed time.

correction.text: It is a fixed proportion. Half of whatever is left decays in each half life, whatever the amount.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The activity of a sample depends on the mass of the sample.

correction.text: It depends on how many nuclei are left, so a larger sample is more active even though the half life is the same.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The length of a moving object is unchanged.

correction.text: It is shortened along the direction of the motion, by the factor the Lorentz factor gives.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: Nothing in the universe can move faster than light.

correction.text: That is true for anything with mass. Light itself travels at the speed of light because it has no mass.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

stem.text: X-rays are produced when high-speed electrons strike a metal target. The characteristic X-rays of an element depend on

explanation.text: The characteristic spectrum of an element is set by the energy levels of its atoms, so it identifies the target material. The speed of the electrons sets the continuous part of the spectrum.

stem.text: How many quantum numbers are needed to describe the state of an electron in an atom?

explanation.text: The four are the principal quantum number $n$, the orbital angular momentum quantum number $\ell$, the magnetic quantum number $m_\ell$ and the spin quantum number $m_s$.

stem.text: The Pauli exclusion principle states that

options.text: two electrons in an atom cannot have the same four quantum numbers
an atom can hold at most two electrons
electrons spin in the same direction
no two atoms can be identical

explanation.text: No two electrons in the same atom can have the same set of four quantum numbers. That is why each orbital holds at most two electrons, and those two must have opposite spins.

options.text: the curvature of spacetime produced by mass and energy
a magnetic effect of the sun
a change in the electric field

explanation.text: In general relativity mass and energy curve spacetime, and bodies follow geodesics in that curved spacetime, which we experience as gravity.

options.text: a loss of predictability after a long time
an increase in the energy of the system
a periodic doubling of the period

explanation.text: In a chaotic system nearby starting points separate exponentially, so the outcome cannot be predicted far ahead even though the laws themselves remain reversible.

stem.text: The most damaging effect of ionising radiation on the body is

options.text: damage to the genetic material in cells
a change in colour of the blood

explanation.text: The danger is that the radiation damages DNA, which can kill cells or cause mutations that become cancers.

options.text: two light nuclei join to form a heavier one
a heavy nucleus splits into lighter ones and releases energy
mass is converted entirely into energy
a nucleus changes its charge without splitting

explanation.text: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei with the release of neutrons and energy.

stem.text: The main difficulty with nuclear fusion as a power source is that

options.text: the nuclei must be brought together against their mutual repulsion at very high temperatures
the reaction cannot be sustained at all

explanation.text: Fusion needs temperatures of millions of kelvin to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between the nuclei, which is why it is hard to sustain.

stem.text: Protons and neutrons are not elementary particles because they are

options.text: not affected by the strong force

explanation.text: Protons and neutrons are each made of three quarks bound by the strong force.

stem.text: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle says that

options.text: a particle's position and momentum cannot both be known precisely
energy is not conserved in quantum systems
the speed of light is variable
electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed paths

explanation.text: The product of the uncertainties in position and momentum has a lower bound set by the reduced Planck constant.

stem.text: The momentum of a photon of wavelength $\lambda$ is

explanation.text: From $E = hf$ and $E = pc$, we get $p = h/\lambda$.

stem.text: The Heisenberg uncertainty principle states that

options.text: the position and the momentum of a particle cannot both be precisely known at the same time
the speed of light is constant

explanation.text: The uncertainty in position and the uncertainty in momentum satisfy $\Delta x \Delta p \geq \hbar/2$, so they cannot both be arbitrarily small.

options.text: light is either a wave or a particle but never both
light and matter show both wave and particle behaviour

explanation.text: Light shows interference and diffraction but also behaves as photons in the photoelectric effect, and matter shows the same duality.

stem.text: In beta decay, a neutron changes into a proton and the nucleus emits

explanation.text: Beta minus decay turns a neutron into a proton and releases an electron and an antineutrino, which is why the atomic number rises by one.

stem.text: The binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus is

options.text: largest for the nuclei near iron and smaller for very heavy nuclei

explanation.text: The curve rises to a maximum near iron and falls again for very heavy nuclei, which is why fission and fusion both release energy.

stem.text: The activity of a sample of radioactive material depends on

options.text: only the number of nuclei present
the number of nuclei and the decay constant

explanation.text: The activity is $A = \lambda N$, so it depends on how many nuclei there are and on the decay constant of the isotope.

stem.text: A rod of proper length $L$ moves at a speed close to the speed of light. Its length measured in the laboratory frame is

explanation.text: Length contraction means the moving rod is measured to be shorter along its direction of motion. Its proper length, measured in its own rest frame, is $L$.

explanation.text: The relativistic momentum is $p = \gamma mv$, with $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$, so it grows faster than $mv$.
